items.title: Pentagon restricts US-Canada military social ties
items.feedTitle: In secret memo, Hegseth restricts U.S.-Canada defense relationship
items.summary: Defense Secretary Hegseth issued a secret memo limiting social and informal interactions between U.S. and Canadian military personnel, according to reporting by The Washington Post and confirmed by Sen. Mike Rounds. The move signals a significant shift in defense relations between the two NATO allies. No official justification has been provided for the restriction.

items.title: Princeton neuroscientist detained by ICE at airport
items.feedTitle: Princeton neuroscientist detained by ICE at D.C. airport after leaving conference
items.summary: A Chinese-born neuroscientist from Princeton University was detained by ICE at Reagan National Airport after returning from a conference. The incident raises concerns about profiling of foreign-born researchers and visa enforcement practices. Details on the basis for the detention remain unclear.

items.title: California rail thieves steal $22 million in organized heists
items.feedTitle: California train burglars carefully executed heists for ‘staggering’ $22m haul
items.summary: Federal authorities arrested 13 suspects in connection with a coordinated theft ring that stole over $22 million in goods from Southern California trains over several years. The operation targeted shipments of Nike sneakers, tools, and other merchandise. Investigators say the burglaries were carefully planned and executed.

items.title: Federal appeals court voids Biden-era spending law
items.feedTitle: Biden-era spending law found unconstitutional by federal appeals court
items.summary: A federal appeals court ruled that a Biden-era spending law was passed unconstitutionally because the House used proxy voting during the 2022 session. The ruling raises questions about the validity of legislation passed during this period. Legal challenges to other bills passed under similar circumstances may follow.

items.title: Major storms threaten both US coasts before Thanksgiving
items.feedTitle: Major storm to bring winds, rain to East Coast ahead of Thanksgiving
items.summary: Powerful storms are expected to impact both coasts ahead of Thanksgiving, with heavy rain and strong winds forecasted for the East Coast and significant tide concerns in California. The San Francisco mayor has urged residents to avoid travel unless essential. Florida continues to deal with record flooding from earlier storms.

stlouis.title: Missouri AG's illegal slot machine ban unraveling
stlouis.feedTitle: Missouri AG barred illegal slot machines. They're still going back into gas stations.
stlouis.summary: Despite Missouri's attorney general barring illegal slot machines, the devices are reportedly being reinstalled in gas stations across the state. The enforcement action appears ineffective in preventing the return of the machines. No details on enforcement plans are yet available.

stlouis.title: St. Louis-based Rawlings gets new majority owner
stlouis.feedTitle: St. Louis-based Rawlings gets new majority owner
stlouis.summary: Rawlings, the sports equipment company based in St. Louis, has announced a new majority ownership stake. The transaction marks a significant change in leadership for the historic sporting goods firm. Details on the new owner's plans remain limited.

stlouis.title: St. Louis rent increased 3.2 percent last year
stlouis.feedTitle: Report: St. Louis rent increased 3.2% last year
stlouis.summary: A new report shows that rental prices in the St. Louis metro area rose 3.2 percent over the past year. The increase reflects broader housing affordability pressures in the region. The data suggests continued upward pressure on housing costs for renters.

items.title: Russia fires missiles into Polish territory; Trump dismisses
items.feedTitle: Poland says Russian missiles hit its territory; Trump calls it a mistake
items.summary: Polish officials say Russian missiles struck Polish territory, but President Trump called the incident a mistake, suggesting it was not intentional. NATO Secretary General Rutte pledged to defend every inch of Polish territory. The incident escalates tensions over the Ukraine war's spillover into NATO airspace.

items.title: Mexican cartel boss 'El Chapo Isidro' captured in raid
items.feedTitle: Alleged Mexican drug cartel boss ‘El Chapo Isidro’ arrested in special forces raid
items.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro' and one of the FBI's 10 most wanted fugitives, was captured by Mexican special forces in a gun battle in Sinaloa that left 11 dead. He led the Beltrán Leyva cartel and later his own organization. The arrest marks a significant blow to drug trafficking operations in northern Mexico.

items.title: Russia launches 400+ drones, missiles at Ukrainian cities
items.feedTitle: Deadly attack in Kyiv as Russia launches barrage against Ukraine
items.summary: Russia launched more than 400 drones and 110 missiles across Ukraine overnight, killing at least seven people in Kyiv. The barrage represents a continuation of sustained attacks on civilian infrastructure. Emergency services responded to multiple strikes across Ukrainian territory.

items.title: Iran strikes Bahrain, escalates regional military tensions
items.feedTitle: Bahrain says Iranian attack hits industrial facility as air defences intercept attacks
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they launched missile and drone attacks on US military positions in Bahrain, claiming to have struck US radars and bases. Bahrain reports a fire at an industrial facility with no reported injuries. Saudi Arabia's air defense reportedly intercepted missiles. The attacks mark an escalation in regional hostilities.

items.title: India posts record 720/9 total in Wellington Test
items.feedTitle: Pant ton drives India to a record 720-9, lead New Zealand by 352
items.summary: India set a historic record by posting a total of 720 for 9 declared against New Zealand in Wellington, their highest-ever Test total in the country. Rishabh Pant scored a century and created more history as the first Indian wicketkeeper to score Test hundreds in all SENA (South Africa, England, New Zealand, Australia) countries. The massive total gives India a commanding lead in the first Test.

items.title: Nine pilgrims killed in Rajasthan highway collision
items.feedTitle: 9 Devotees, Returning From Khatu Shyam Temple, Killed As Their Vehicle Rams Parked Truck In Rajasthan's Kota
items.summary: Nine devotees returning from Khatu Shyam Temple in Rajasthan were killed when their vehicle rammed a parked truck on the Kota-Udaipur highway. The group, primarily from Maharashtra, died in the collision. Several others were injured in the accident.

items.title: Illicit alcohol kills 11, poisons 180 in Manipur
items.feedTitle: Illicit alcohol kills 11, poisons 180 in northeast India’s Manipur state
items.summary: At least 11 people died and around 180 others were hospitalized after consuming spurious liquor in Manipur, India's northeast state. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi blamed negligence of the BJP government for the tragedy. The incident highlights ongoing public health concerns related to illegal alcohol production.

items.title: India launches indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine
items.feedTitle: Union Minister launches India’s first indigenous H5N1 bird flu vaccine
items.summary: India's Union Minister launched the country's first domestically developed H5N1 bird flu vaccine. The development marks a significant step in India's efforts to address avian influenza threats. Local production of the vaccine is expected to improve accessibility and reduce dependence on imports.

items.title: 14-year-old hacker arrested for Agniveer data theft
items.feedTitle: 14-year-old hacker held for trying to sell private data of 4,000 Agniveers on dark web: Delhi Police
items.summary: Delhi Police apprehended a 14-year-old who allegedly used an AI chatbot to hack into the Agniveer recruitment test website to steal personal data of approximately 4,000 Agniveers. The teenager reportedly attempted to sell the data on the dark web. Sources say the minor used AI assistance to execute the hack.

immigration.title: H-1B visa issuances plunge one-third under Trump
immigration.feedTitle: H-1B Visa Issuances Plunge by a Third; IBM Leads Pullback in Sponsoring Consulting Division Visas
immigration.summary: H-1B visa issuances have dropped by approximately one-third, with major tech employers like IBM pulling back on sponsoring consulting division visas. The decline reflects proposed and finalized Trump administration restrictions on the program, including proposed changes to end deference to prior approvals. The trend is driving some skilled workers to seek opportunities in other countries like the UK.

immigration.title: H-1B visa barriers drive tech workers to UK exits
immigration.feedTitle: US feels like a golden prison: Google engineer on H-1B visa says he's moving to the UK without a job, say
immigration.summary: Rising H-1B visa restrictions and Trump's rule changes are pushing skilled tech workers on H-1B status to leave the United States, with some moving to the UK without immediate job offers. Workers report feeling the U.S. is becoming a 'golden prison' due to visa uncertainty and sponsorship barriers. The exodus represents a loss of talent for U.S. tech companies already facing uncertainty over visa policy changes.

items.title: AI boom cracks, dragging S&P 500 into correction
items.feedTitle: AI Boom Cracks, Unleashing US Stock Selloff as S&P 500 and Dow Both Slip Below Correction Line
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average have both slipped into correction territory as worries about artificial intelligence valuations and profitability trigger a broad market sell-off. The Nasdaq has erased all 2026 gains. Tech stocks, particularly those in AI and semiconductors, have been hit hardest as investors reassess the costs and returns of massive AI buildout.

items.title: SEC reportedly investigating Nvidia's accounting practices
items.feedTitle: Nvidia faces US accounting probe amid deepening turmoil: media
items.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission is reportedly investigating Nvidia's accounting practices amid the company's $2.5 trillion stock rout. The probe raises questions about financial reporting standards at the chip giant during the AI boom. Nvidia has not publicly commented on the investigation.

items.title: Indian stocks surge against global market downturn
items.feedTitle: Indian Stocks Surge Against Global Market Tide as Nifty 50 Nears Record High on Foreign Inflows of Over 1 Trillion Rupees
items.summary: While global markets tumble, the Nifty 50 and Sensex have extended their winning streak to four weeks, hitting nine-month highs on record foreign institutional investor buying of over 1 trillion rupees. India's AI-free market positioning is attracting foreign capital as investors seek alternatives to AI-heavy U.S. stocks. Bank Nifty has surged nearly 17.5% in just one month.

items.title: Bayer settles Roundup cancer suits for $7.25 billion
items.feedTitle: Bayer reaches Roundup settlement that could cost the company billions
items.summary: A federal judge approved Bayer's $7.25 billion settlement to resolve approximately 65,000 lawsuits alleging that its Roundup weedkiller causes cancer. The settlement potentially resolves litigation that has weighed heavily on the German company. This marks a significant conclusion to one of the largest product liability cases in recent years.

items.title: Market sell-off accelerates as Goldman warns of danger
items.feedTitle: Goldman Sachs admits the 'AI unwind' has spiraled into something more dangerous — and it's watching for 3 signs of bottom
items.summary: Goldman Sachs said the AI-driven stock selloff has spiraled beyond an ordinary market correction, with the bank watching for three signs of a bottom in what it calls a dangerous 'AI unwind.' The S&P 500 is having its longest losing streak since February 2020. Market volatility has intensified as investors question the profitability and valuation of massive AI infrastructure investments.

cards.title: The Default Path Trap
cards.insight: We often continue habits because they're the path of least resistance—not because they serve us. When markets tumble or personal circumstances shift, the default habit suddenly feels wrong, forcing conscious choice. Real change rarely starts with willpower; it starts when the status quo becomes obviously misaligned with reality.
cards.takeaway: Before trying to change a habit, identify what makes it currently 'easy.' Then ask: has that reason still valid, or am I coasting?

cards.title: Verification Before Celebration
cards.insight: Anthropic's claim to have solved a 165-year-old math problem generated immediate praise, but competing approaches and verification requirements quickly followed. Early wins often feel validating, but premature celebration can mask gaps. Lasting behavioral change requires the unglamorous work of verification and adjustment, not just hitting a milestone.
cards.takeaway: When you hit a goal or see early success, pause to gather real feedback—not just external validation—before declaring victory.

cards.title: Risk Cascades from Automation
cards.insight: Anthropic engineers are now warning that AI-driven automation of infrastructure fixes could backfire, introducing new vulnerabilities faster than humans spot them. Similarly, automating habits (apps, routines, delegation) can create dependencies and blind spots. The convenience of automation can mask the loss of control.
cards.takeaway: For habits you automate, build in regular check-ins to ensure the automation still serves your actual needs, not just your original intent.

cards.title: The Herd Reversal
cards.insight: Investors poured $45.7 billion into stock funds the week before markets crashed, then watched Anthropic's historic IPO collapse during the worst tech week since 2020. Mass behavior—buying into trends, following consensus—often peaks just before reversals. For habits, this means popular diets, viral routines, and everyone-is-doing-it changes often carry hidden fragility.
cards.takeaway: When a habit or behavior trend feels universally popular, it's time to stress-test your personal commitment to it independent of the crowd.

ai.title: Anthropic mathematician claims Riemann hypothesis solved
ai.feedTitle: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
ai.summary: A mathematician at Anthropic says he used the company's Claude AI to help prove the Riemann hypothesis, one of mathematics' most important unsolved problems, after six weeks of work. Two independent groups have begun verifying the claim, though a competing all-human draft proof from Stanford emerged hours after the announcement. Full verification is expected to take time.

ai.title: Anthropic IPO collides with worst tech week since 2020
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic’s record IPO collides with tech’s worst week on Wall Street since 2020
ai.summary: Anthropic's record-breaking IPO debut as the second-largest in U.S. history occurred during the worst week for technology stocks since the COVID-19 pandemic, as investors reassess the costs and returns of AI buildout. The company's shares have dropped significantly despite strong initial demand. The timing highlights broader concerns about AI valuations amid slowing momentum.

ai.title: Anthropic engineer warns Claude Code poses risks
ai.feedTitle: Anthropic engineer's warning about Claude Code explains why tech outages could get much worse
ai.summary: An Anthropic engineer has warned that Claude Code, the company's AI tool for writing and executing code, could make tech outages more common by enabling AI systems to autonomously fix security flaws in ways that introduce new vulnerabilities. The warning raises concerns about automated AI-driven changes to critical systems. The issue highlights broader safety questions about AI autonomy in infrastructure.

ai.title: UC system signs systemwide deal with OpenAI
ai.feedTitle: UC jumps into AI with systemwide OpenAI deal as faculty urge caution
ai.summary: The University of California system has announced a system-wide agreement with OpenAI, while faculty members have urged caution about the partnership. The deal aims to integrate AI tools across UC campuses. Some academics have expressed concerns about data privacy and over-reliance on proprietary AI systems.

ai.title: Etsy faces backlash over AI model training inclusion
ai.feedTitle: Etsy faces backlash over including AI model training in new policy update
ai.summary: Etsy has faced significant user backlash after updating its policies to include AI model training, allowing the company to use seller content for AI purposes. The policy change has sparked concerns among the platform's creator community about intellectual property and fair compensation. The controversy reflects broader tension between platforms and content creators over AI training data.
